phase_task.goal: Wrap the owned core in the API-only consumer surface: authentication on every endpoint, the POST /v1/tasks contract with SSE progress streaming, server-side budget enforcement that stops cleanly, and per-user/per-task metering. This is where hard requirement #1 (API is the only door — index, sandbox, model unreachable by any consumer) becomes real and testable. The agent brain (Phases 1–5) is wired IN behind this layer, unchanged in contract.

deliverables.d: Auth on EVERY consumer endpoint: hashed API keys (the Phase-0 issue/verify path), constant-time compare, Authorization: Bearer <key>. Unauthenticated or bad-key requests get 401 before any work. Per-key rate limit. The authenticated user identity is the ONLY source of the (user_id) used for isolation — never a client-supplied user_id.

POST /v1/tasks per the spec contract: body { workspace_id, instruction, budget:{max_tokens,max_usd,max_wall_seconds}, mode:"apply"|"dry_run" } -> 202 Accepted { task_id, events }. The task runs asynchronously (the Phase-4/5 loop) against the caller's OWN workspace only — a workspace_id the caller does not own resolves to NotFound (isolation by construction, not a filter). dry_run returns a patch and commits nothing; apply commits a verified change.

SSE GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/events: stream the loop's progress events (plan, steps, tool calls, verification results) and the terminal state, for the caller's own task only. Reading another user's task -> NotFound. GET /v1/tasks/{task_id} returns current status + terminal state + metering summary.

Server-side budget enforcement wired to the request budget: the loop's existing reserve/commit ledger discipline is fed the per-task budget from the request; a task hitting max_tokens / max_usd / max_wall_seconds stops at a clean journaled checkpoint in budget-exhausted state, reports partial progress, workspace uncorrupted. max_usd uses the (placeholder-flagged) price constants -> cost. The consumer cannot override server-side enforcement.

Metering surfaced per user and per task: tokens in/out, tool calls, retrieval bytes, sandbox seconds — from the ledger/task rows — returned in the status response and aggregated per user. Choose defensible dimensions; this feeds the Phase-7 $/task story.

Repoint the carried seam: /readyz now checks the REAL sandbox runner's healthy() (build_sandbox_client from settings), not the StubSandboxClient — so readiness reflects actual Docker availability. Keep the stub path only for in-process unit tests that explicitly inject it.

API-only boundary enforced structurally: NO consumer-reachable route to the index, the sandbox, or the model. The only endpoints exposed are the /v1/tasks surface + health/metrics. Assert there is no path (route, param, or passthrough) that lets a consumer query the raw index, shell the sandbox, or reach the model directly.

phase_task.oracle: Via make test (unit + integration; Docker for the end-to-end verified task): (1) AUTH — a request with no key or a bad key to any /v1 endpoint returns 401 and does no work; a valid key succeeds; assert constant-time compare and hashed storage (no raw key persisted). (2) ISOLATION — user A calling POST /v1/tasks or GET events/status with user B's workspace_id/task_id gets NotFound (not 403-that-leaks-existence, not another user's data); the user_id used is derived from the key, and a client-supplied user_id is ignored. (3) CONTRACT — POST /v1/tasks returns 202 + task_id + events URL; the task runs the real loop and reaches verified-success ONLY via the real sandbox; dry_run returns a patch and commits nothing (assert base workspace unchanged); apply commits the verified change. (4) SSE — the events stream emits plan/step/verify/terminal events for the owner and NotFound for a non-owner. (5) BUDGET — a task with a tiny max_tokens (or max_wall_seconds) stops in budget-exhausted at a clean checkpoint, reports partial progress, workspace uncorrupted, no overrun past the limit; the consumer cannot disable enforcement. (6) API-ONLY — assert (by route inventory + a negative test) there is NO consumer endpoint that reaches the index/sandbox/model directly. (7) /readyz reflects the REAL sandbox healthy() now. Each clause evidenced by its actual mechanism.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md: the API/gateway section — the /v1 contract, the auth model (hashed keys, why API keys over JWT/mTLS for this deliverable, with the others noted), and how the API-only boundary is structural (the only door). Extend the isolation section: server-side user_id from the key, workspace/task ownership as NotFound-not-filter. Finalize the metering section with the dimensions actually surfaced and how max_usd is computed (noting the placeholder prices). Note the /readyz repoint. Update the DESIGN.md "auth on every endpoint" and "budgets enforced server-side" hard-requirement claims to point at the tests that prove them.
phase_task.stop: Do not start Phase 7 (eval harness + full pyramid + docs finalize). Report: the /v1 endpoint inventory with the auth guard on each; how the authenticated user_id flows into isolation (and how a client-supplied user_id is ignored); the POST /v1/tasks apply vs dry_run behavior; how the request budget reaches the loop's server-side enforcement and how a clean budget stop is reached; the metering dimensions surfaced; the /readyz repoint to the real sandbox; and the assertion/test proving no consumer path reaches index/sandbox/model.
